newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares firm on strengthening dollar, bonds.
newsitem.headline: German shares firm on strengthening dollar, bonds.

text.p: Germany's IBIS DAX index traded higher on Wednesday, shrugging off a slightly weaker close on Wall Street overnight. Market sentiment was lifted by the strengthening dollar and underpinned by firmer German debt.
At 0756 GMT the IBIS DAX index was up 11.18 points at 3,570.47 points, while the June DAX future contract was at 3,580 points, up 16.

"The dollar is picking up and that is helping to support the market. To be honest I think we need to see a bit of profit-taking, a bit of consolidation. The market feels a bit toppy at the moment," a trader said.

The market of late has been trading in or around record levels and traders said there was evidence that of a touch of vertigo at these heights without solid fundamentals to back up the bullish sentiment.

The main focus of share trade in the morning was Deutsche Telekom, which fell after German newspaper Handelsblatt reported in its Wednesday edition the Bonn government might consider selling some if its Telekom shares.
The paper reported that the Bonn government wants to sell a portion of its nearly 75 percent stake in Telekom this year as part of efforts to pare back the budget deficit.
The news drove the shares nearly four and a half percent lower at one point, but the share recovered somewhat and was trading at 38.98 marks,was down 85 pfennigs, or 2.09 percent, at 38.92 marks.

"I think that today we are going to see a Telekom bourse, but the market is proving resistant," a Frankfurt trader said, adding and said that volumes were enormous early on, but that 38 marks was proving to be a point of massive resistance.
The trader said that if it was true that Bonn was planning to sell off the share, then the earnings potential for the Telekom share was limited.
However, dealers insisted that the fundamental figures for Telekom remained good. "All in all, I think the market could well absorb a big block of Telekom shares," the trader said.
Other traders were sceptical whether Bonn would actually bring the shares to market in the end. "We're also seeing more buyers than sellers at the lower levels," said one trader.
BASF and Schering both benefited from the higher dollar. BASF was up 1.29 percent at 68.10 marks, while Schering was up 1.69 percent at 57 marks.
Volkswagen performed best among the car stocks, up 1.26 percent at 165 marks.

Finance stocks were also in favour pre-bourse. Deutsche Bank was up 1.45 marks, or 1.51 percent at 97.67 marks, Commerzbank was up 65 pfennigs or 1.36 percent at 48.30 marks while Dresdner was up 78 pfennigs, or 1.33 percent, at 59.38 marks.
